- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust upward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.5), model tends to over-forecast; adjust downward by 1–3%.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak if sentiment remains bullish.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in late-cycle trends; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral, add 2–5% upward bias to correct for lag.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate true price if sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply smoothing filter to reduce overreaction to short-term sentiment swings.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.33 → -0.33 → +0.33), model often misses the reversal; add 1–2% downward bias in next forecast.
